task.description: Bring the page to life with jQuery. 1) A click on #like-btn increases the number in #like-count by 1 (the variable let likes = 0 is outside the handler). 2) A click on #theme-toggle toggles the class theme-dark on body and sets the button's aria-pressed to "true" or "false". 3) Deleting with delegation: one handler $("#todo-list").on("click", ".item__delete", ...) deletes the whole li.item whose button was clicked and writes "Items: 2" into #items-count (the number is how many items are left). Items added after the page loads must be deleted too. 4) When the user types in #comment, #comment-counter shows "12 / 100", and if there are more than 90 characters, #comment-counter has the class is-warning. Handlers only through .on(); do not use .click(fn), addEventListener, onclick, innerHTML, .html() or .style.

tests.name: One click on "Like" → 1
tests.fail: In the handler, increase likes and write it into #like-count: $likeCount.text(likes);

tests.name: Three clicks → 3
tests.check: (() => { const b = document.querySelector("#like-btn"); b.click(); b.click(); b.click(); return document.querySelector("#like-count").textContent === "3"; })()
tests.fail: Declare let likes = 0; OUTSIDE the handler, otherwise the count starts over every time.

tests.name: Theme: the first click turns on theme-dark and aria-pressed="true"
tests.check: (() => { const b = document.querySelector("#theme-toggle"); b.click(); return document.body.classList.contains("theme-dark") && b.getAttribute("aria-pressed") === "true"; })()

tests.name: Theme: the second click turns it off
tests.check: (() => { const b = document.querySelector("#theme-toggle"); b.click(); b.click(); return !document.body.classList.contains("theme-dark") && b.getAttribute("aria-pressed") === "false"; })()
tests.fail: Use toggleClass, not addClass, and set aria-pressed from the new state.

tests.name: The "Delete" button removes the whole item
tests.check: (() => { document.querySelectorAll(".item__delete")[0].click(); const texts = [...document.querySelectorAll("#todo-list .item__text")].map((s) => s.textContent); return document.querySelectorAll("#todo-list .item").length === 2 && texts[0] === "Complete lesson 6" && texts[1] === "Submit the IDE task"; })()
tests.fail: Delete the item, not the button: $(this).closest(".item").remove();

tests.name: After deleting: "Items: 2"
tests.fail: After remove(), count the items: $list.children(".item").length - and write the number into #items-count.

tests.name: An item added after loading is deleted too (delegation)
tests.check:
(() => { $("#todo-list").append("
  • New item
    • "); const btns = document.querySelectorAll(".item__delete"); btns[btns.length - 1].click(); return document.querySelectorAll("#todo-list .item").length === 3 && ![...document.querySelectorAll(".item__text")].some((s) => s.textContent === "New item"); })()
tests.fail: Attach ONE handler with a selector to #todo-list: $list.on("click", ".item__delete", function () { ... }); - then new items work too.

tests.name: A click on the item text deletes nothing
tests.fail: The second argument of .on() is the selector ".item__delete": the handler must fire only on the buttons.

tests.name: All items deleted: "Items: 0"
tests.check: (() => { for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { document.querySelector(".item__delete").click(); } return document.querySelectorAll("#todo-list .item").length === 0 && document.querySelector("#items-count").textContent === "Items: 0" && __error === null; })()
tests.fail: Count the items again after each deletion instead of decreasing the number by hand.

tests.name: Character counter: "JavaScript" → "10 / 100"
tests.check: (() => { (() => { const c = document.querySelector("#comment"); c.value = "JavaScript"; c.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); })(); return document.querySelector("#comment-counter").textContent === "10 / 100"; })()

tests.name: The counter goes back to "0 / 100" when the field is cleared
tests.check: (() => { (() => { const c = document.querySelector("#comment"); c.value = "Hello"; c.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); })(); (() => { const c = document.querySelector("#comment"); c.value = ""; c.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); })(); return document.querySelector("#comment-counter").textContent === "0 / 100"; })()
tests.fail: Take the length from the field's current value on every input event.

tests.name: Class is-warning: present at 95 and 98 characters, absent at 5
tests.check: (() => { const p = document.querySelector("#comment-counter"); (() => { const c = document.querySelector("#comment"); c.value = "a".repeat(95); c.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); })(); const a = p.classList.contains("is-warning"); (() => { const c = document.querySelector("#comment"); c.value = "a".repeat(98); c.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); })(); const b = p.classList.contains("is-warning"); (() => { const c = document.querySelector("#comment"); c.value = "a".repeat(5); c.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); })(); const c = p.classList.contains("is-warning"); return a && b && !c; })()
tests.fail: Pass the state as the second argument: .toggleClass("is-warning", length > 90). Without it, the class simply toggles on every input.

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: Check the selectors and make sure you use $(this) inside handlers, not this.text().

hints: Likes: let likes = 0; outside, and inside the handler likes++ and $likeCount.text(likes);
Delegation: $list.on("click", ".item__delete", function () { ... }); - inside it, this is the clicked button.
Do not use an arrow function if you need $(this) inside.

questions.question: Which code subscribes a button to clicks in the course style?
questions.explanation: .on() is the main subscription method. Shortcuts like .click(fn) and .bind() are deprecated.

questions.question: What is this inside the handler $(".card").on("click", function () { ... })?
options: A jQuery object with all the cards
The DOM element of the card that was clicked
questions.explanation: this is an ordinary DOM element. To call jQuery methods, wrap it: $(this).

questions.question: Why does nothing get deleted in the handler $list.on("click", ".del", () => { $(this).closest("li").remove(); })?
options: An arrow function has no this of its own - $(this) is not the button
You need to write .click instead of .on
remove() works only with an id
questions.explanation: An arrow function takes this from the outside. Use function () { ... } or event.currentTarget.

questions.question: What advantages does the delegation $list.on("click", ".item__delete", fn) give?
options: It works for items added after the page loads
One handler instead of a handler on each button
questions.explanation: The handler is attached to the list, which always exists, and checks which element the event came from.

questions.question: Match an event object property with its meaning in the delegation $("#list").on("click", ".item__delete", ...) when an icon inside the button was clicked.
questions.explanation: target is the deepest element, currentTarget (and this) is the element that matched the selector, delegateTarget is the element .on() is attached to.

questions.question: What does event.preventDefault() do in a click handler on a link?
questions.explanation: preventDefault cancels the browser's default action. Bubbling is stopped by stopPropagation.

questions.question: Which method removes a handler attached with .on()? Enter the method name without the dot and brackets.
questions.explanation: $el.off("click") removes click handlers, and $el.off("click.menu") removes only those from the menu namespace.

questions.question: How many times will the handler $("#ok").one("click", fn) fire if you click the button three times?
questions.explanation: .one() attaches a handler that removes itself after it fires for the first time.

questions.question: Which events are suitable for a live character counter in a field?
questions.explanation: input fires on any change of the value (including pasting with the mouse) - it is the best choice. keydown also fires while typing, but before the value changes, and it does not catch pasting with the mouse; change fires only after leaving the field.

questions.question: What does $("#like-btn").trigger("click") do?
options: Fires a click from code, and the handlers run
Nothing: trigger works only with forms
questions.explanation: .trigger() fires an event programmatically - handy for tests and for reusing a handler.

questions.question: Match the code with the result.
pairs: A handler in the menu namespace
All handlers of the menu namespace are removed
return false in a jQuery handler
Key presses on the whole page
questions.explanation: A namespace lets you remove only your own handlers without touching other people's.

questions.question: Complete the condition so that the handler closes the window only on Escape: if (event.key === "..."). Enter only the value without quotes.
questions.explanation: event.key contains the name of the key: "Escape", "Enter", "ArrowUp".
